result.rationale: The diff confirms the mechanism: `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` swallows the error (not even logging err) and the handler proceeds to `return { message: "Guests added" }`, which triggers the client's `showToast(t("guests_added"), "success")`. So on email failure the user is told guests were added via email while notifications silently never went out — a real silent-failure defect introduced by this diff, accurately described by the finding.

judged_text: Email-send failures are caught and reduced to console.log('Error sending AddGuestsEmails') while the mutation returns { message: 'Guests added' }. When sendAddGuestsEmails fails (SMTP outage, renderEmail throw, unbounded replyTo rejection), the organizer and all attendees receive no notification and no updated ICS, yet the user sees the 'Guests added' success toast — the failure is completely invisible to the user and unobservable beyond a server console line with no error object logged.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that swallows all errors and only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` without logging the error object, while the mutation still returns success (`{ message: "Guests added" }`) and the UI shows a success toast on `onSuccess`. This is a diff-grounded observability/UX issue (email notification failure becomes invisible), but the core mutation (DB update + `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`) still succeeds, so it’s not a strictly verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone.
